Record date: 2129-08-14
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 08/14/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Increased shortness of breath, persistent cough, and worsening lower extremity edema.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for follow-up after one week of the intensified treatment regimen. He reports that his shortness of breath has worsened, particularly at rest, and he continues to experience a productive cough with yellow-green sputum that has not improved. The patient notes that the increased furosemide has provided minimal relief for his bilateral lower extremity edema, which he describes as now extending to the thighs and is accompanied by discomfort.
He expresses concern over his persistent fatigue, which he attributes to both his respiratory issues and the inability to achieve restful sleep. Mr. Fairfax states that he has followed the sleep hygiene recommendations but has not found any significant improvement in his insomnia. He denies any new fever but continues to experience chills and malaise.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, - weight gain, + chills, - night sweats. Pulmonary - + worsening shortness of breath at rest, + productive cough with yellow-green sputum, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + worsening bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 155/92 mmHg - Heart Rate: 90 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 26 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 85% on room air
General: The patient appears fatigued and is in significant respiratory distress, using accessory muscles for breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring, oropharynx clear.
Lungs: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally with pronounced wheezing; bilateral crackles and rhonchi present throughout.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops.
Extremities: Severe bilateral lower extremity edema with pitting, extending to the thighs, with tenderness noted on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation with inadequate response to current treatment; ongoing sputum production raises concern for possible pneumonia or other pulmonary infection. 2. Congestive heart failure with worsening fluid overload; current diuretic therapy remains insufficient to manage edema. 3. Persistent insomnia with inadequate response to trazodone; further evaluation needed for possible sleep disorders.
PLAN
1. Obtain a chest X-ray to assess for pneumonia or other pulmonary complications, given the increased sputum production and respiratory distress. 2. Initiate a course of oral prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days to reduce airway inflammation and improve respiratory symptoms. 3. Increase furosemide to 320 mg daily, with close monitoring of renal function and electrolytes, particularly potassium levels, and consider adding spironolactone if needed for resistant edema. 4. Continue nebulized albuterol every 2 hours and nebulized budesonide every 6 hours; consider adding ipratropium bromide for additional bronchodilation. 5. Refer Mr. Fairfax for a sleep study to evaluate for obstructive sleep apnea and consider alternative medications such as zolpidem or ramelteon for insomnia management. 6. Reiterate the importance of medication adherence and monitoring for signs of worsening respiratory or cardiac symptoms, including daily weight checks to monitor fluid status.
Mr. Fairfax demonstrated understanding of the treatment plan and expressed willingness to adhere to the recommendations.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was stable for discharge, with a follow-up appointment scheduled for 08/21/29. He was advised to seek immediate medical attention if he experiences any acute changes, including increased shortness of breath, chest pain, or significant weight gain.
